title: The covenant of circumcision
hook: a baby boy's circumcision on the eighth day

segments.voice: Yesterday's line was welcome: a blessing, friends at the house, and baruch haba at the door. Who did you greet out loud? Today, the ceremony that greeting so often opens. Day one thousand two hundred ninety-three.

A room full of people, on the eighth day after a birth. Grandparents, cousins, a few friends who took the morning off. Near the front stands an empty chair that nobody sits in. The baby is carried in on a pillow, and the room calls out: baruch haba. One person, a grandfather perhaps, or an honored friend, settles in to hold the child on his lap. Another, trained for exactly this, steps forward. Then come blessings, a name spoken aloud for the first time, a little wine, and food. Today's word is the name of that morning.
screen: `THE EIGHTH DAY.` → `AN EMPTY CHAIR.` → `A NAME SPOKEN ALOUD.`

segments.voice: Brit milah. Brit means covenant; milah means circumcision. The covenant of circumcision. Turn it four ways. First, the command and its day. In Genesis, God makes a covenant with Abraham, and it is to be carried in the body. The old Jewish Publication Society translation reads: "And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you." The eighth day is so central that the Talmud teaches it goes ahead even on Shabbat. But a baby's health comes first: if the child is unwell, the brit waits. Second, the people. The one who performs it is called a mohel. The one who holds the baby is the sandak, a place of honor. And the empty chair belongs to Elijah the prophet. Tradition says Elijah once complained that Israel had abandoned the covenant, so he is invited to every brit, to see for himself that it goes on. Third, the words. The father, or both parents, bless God for the command to bring the child into the covenant of Abraham. And the guests answer with a line from the liturgy: as he has entered the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the wedding canopy, and good deeds. Learning, love, kindness. A whole life, wished for in one breath. Fourth, the name. At the brit, the boy's Hebrew name is announced for the first time, as son of his father, and in some families his mother too. The covenant is the frame; the name is what goes inside it.
screen: `EIGHT DAYS OLD.` · `MOHEL, SANDAK, AND ELIJAH'S CHAIR.` · `TORAH, CANOPY, GOOD DEEDS.` · `THE NAME IS SPOKEN.` · then, large: `THE COVENANT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn what happens at a brit, slowly. Settle, and breathe. Walk through it in your mind, one step per breath. The baby carried in, and the room saying baruch haba. Elijah's chair, empty. The sandak, holding. The blessing for the covenant of Abraham. The guests' wish: Torah, the canopy, good deeds. The name, spoken for the first time. Then let the last image rest: a whole room promising to stand behind one small person. If you pray, you can pray for a child you love. The bell holds the time.
Brit milah. The covenant of circumcision: the eighth day, Elijah's chair, the guests' wish, and the name. Today's word.
Your line: the covenant. Today, notice one promise that holds you to other people, one you didn't choose but still keep. Day one thousand two hundred ninety-three.

howItsDone: Many Jewish families hold a brit milah on the eighth day after a boy's birth, with a mohel performing the circumcision, a sandak holding the baby, blessings, the announcement of his Hebrew name, and a festive meal.

what a scholar hears: Genesis 17, the covenant carried in the body; the Talmud lets it override Shabbat, but never the child's health.
